To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the sterolwax ester fraction contained more linoleic and less arachidonic and methyl 11-eocosanoic acids, and the mono- and digly- ceride fraction contained more stearate and less lignoceric acid in carcinomas than in normal or hyperplasic epidermis.

the sterolwax ester fraction from carcinomas contained much more linoleate and much less arachidate than did normal or abnormal epidermis, and the mono- and diglyceroide fraction from carcinomas had a higher level of stearic acid.

The sterol-waxes from normal and hyperplasic epidermis did differ, but the most interesting finding was that the carcinomas were more unsaturated than normal or hyperplasic epidernis and contained more arachidonic and linoleic acids than did the other fractions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the chemical nature of sterol-wax and mono- and di- glyceride fractions of mouse epidermis undergoing normal and abnormal growth changes.
the lipid composition of the epidermis of mice, particularly the fatty acid composition of the sterol-waxes and mono- and di-glycerides.
the fatty acid composition of the sterol-waxy ester and mono-and diglyceride fractions from normal, hyperplastic, and carcinogen-induced epidermal tissue.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, in the epidermis, the fatty acid composition of the sterol-waxes is not affected by the growth rate of the tissue; however, the mono- and diglyeride fractions of hyperplastic epidemis differ from those of normal epidermis in having a higher level of stearic acid.
, following pluckings, normal and hyperplasic epidermis did differ in the fatty acid composition of the sterol-was ester fraction.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the sterolwax ester fraction from carcinomas was more unsaturated and contained more arachidonic and linoleic acids than did the sterol-waxes of normal or hyperplasic epidermis.
the fatty acid composition of the sterol-waxes and monoglyceroles of epidermal carcinomas is significantly altered from that of normal epidermis.
the sterolwax ester fraction from normal epidermal tissue was composed of 60–65% saturated fatty acids, 30–35% unsaturated fatty acids, and 5–10% methyl-branched fatty acids.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the sterolwax ester fraction is the most useful for differentiating carcinomas from normal or hyper-plastic epidermis.
the fatty acid composition of the sterolwax ester and monoglyceride fractions of the epidermis is not altered significantly by plucking, but is markedly changed by the carcinogenic process.

the fatty acid composition of the sterol-waxes ester and mono-and diglyceride fractions of epidermal lipid is altered in the presence of carcinogenic agents and in the presence of hyperplastic growth changes.
